---
title: 'Configure pipelines'
status: implemented
description: 'Set up what a pipeline builds, from the UI or from .oore.yaml, and which parts stay in Oore.'
---

A pipeline tells Oore what to build for a project, with which credentials and
under which rules. What it builds can come from settings saved in Oore or
from a `.oore.yaml` file in the repository. Credentials, approvals and
per-workflow overrides always stay in Oore. Read
[Files, pipelines and workflows](/concepts/files-pipelines-workflows) for
which part lives where.

## Set up a pipeline

- [Configure a pipeline in the UI](/build/pipelines/use-the-ui) from a
  template, without a file.
- [Move a pipeline into `.oore.yaml`](/build/pipelines/oore-yaml) so it changes
  with the code.
- [Add pipelines from the repository](/build/pipelines/from-the-repository):
  let Oore turn the config files it finds into pipelines, and check each
  pipeline's health.

## Work with workflows

- [Run two workflows from one file](/build/pipelines/two-workflows), such as an
  ad hoc build for testers and a store release, each with its own signing and
  publishing.
- [Move credentials into the project library](/build/sign/project-library) so
  each workflow signs with its own keys.

## Inputs and rules

- [Use secrets in a pipeline](/build/pipelines/secrets) for tokens and keys.
- [Set triggers, timeouts, and approvals](/build/pipelines/triggers).

- [`.oore.yaml` version 2](/reference/config/oore-yaml-v2)
